description.content:
Defines a new custom industry Aggregation Scheme from a set of groupings. Custom schemes are
built asynchronously and take time to process - the new scheme cannot be used to run impacts
until its `status` becomes `"Complete"`. Use `GetAggregationScheme` to poll the
scheme's details and status. Industry codes that are not placed in a group are added to the

of these characters: `|;%*?!='"^#`. The scheme description is also required, must be unique for
the user, and must not contain a comma. Sector codes must not be duplicated across groups.

item.name: Builds a single combined Region model.

request.name: Builds a single combined Region model.

description.content:
Combines two or more Regions (by URID/HashId) into a single Region and builds it. This is the
single-request form of `BuildCombinedRegionBatch`.

The model builds in the background: this call returns the Region with `modelBuildStatus``"New"`, and the build is not finished until `modelBuildStatus` becomes `"Complete"`.
Poll `GetUserRegion` (by HashId) to watch the status - do not poll the heavy
`GetEconomicIndustryData` / `GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` reads to detect readiness; they
return an error until the model is `Complete`. Builds typically finish within a few minutes;
poll roughly every 15 seconds.

At least one Region identifier is required. When combining more than one Region: a description/name
is required and must be unique for the user, the Region identifiers must be distinct, all Regions
must come from the same dataset, and no Region may overlap or nest within another. A configured
maximum number of Regions per combined model is enforced.
(Required) The Aggregation Scheme the combined Region belongs to.

item.name: Builds a Region model with customized average RPC data.

request.name: Builds a Region model with customized average RPC data.

description.content:
Builds a new model from an existing Region (identified by exactly one of HashId, URID, or
UserModelId) with user-supplied average RPC (Regional Purchase Coefficient) data applied. Only the
commodities being customized need to be supplied. Use `GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` to obtain
the starting values.

The model builds in the background: this call returns the Region with `modelBuildStatus``"New"` and is not finished until `modelBuildStatus` becomes `"Complete"`. Poll
`GetUserRegion` (by HashId) to watch the status - do not poll
`GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` to detect readiness; it returns an error until the model is
`Complete`. Poll roughly every 15 seconds.

The average-RPC fields are interdependent - supply a mutually consistent, full-precision set (start
from `GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` and scale the coupled fields together); `averageRpc`
cannot be set alone. These relationships must hold (each is checked; a violation returns 422):
- `averageRpc = localUseOfLocalSupply / totalGrossCommodityDemand`.
- `localUseRatio = localUseOfLocalSupply / totalCommoditySupply` (checked to tight float precision - a rounded ratio will fail).
- `localUseOfLocalSupply` may not exceed the local domestic commodity demand / local net commodity supply, so a commodity's RPC can effectively only be lowered (or raised only slightly).

The Region's description/name must not contain an ampersand or any of these characters:
`|;%*?!='"^#`, and must be unique for the user. At least one commodity must be supplied, only
modifiable commodities can be customized, and foreign imports/exports cannot be changed.
(Required) The Aggregation Scheme the model belongs to.

item.name: Builds a Region model with customized industry data.

request.name: Builds a Region model with customized industry data.

description.content:
Builds a new model from an existing Region (identified by exactly one of HashId, URID, or
UserModelId) with user-supplied industry data applied. Only the industries being customized need to
be supplied, but every field must be provided for each. Use `GetEconomicIndustryData` to obtain
the starting values.

The model builds in the background: this call returns the Region with `modelBuildStatus``"New"` and is not finished until `modelBuildStatus` becomes `"Complete"`. Poll
`GetUserRegion` (by HashId) to watch the status - do not poll
`GetEconomicIndustryData` to detect readiness; it returns an error until the model is
`Complete`. Poll roughly every 15 seconds.

The Region's description/name must not contain an ampersand or any of these characters:
`|;%*?!='"^#`, and must be unique for the user. At least one customized industry must be
supplied, and the base model must not already have a history of industry-production or average-RPC
customizations. Per customized industry: Employment cannot be positive when Output is zero; Employee
Compensation and Proprietor Income cannot be positive when Employment is zero; and the sum of
Employee Compensation, Proprietor Income, Other Property Income, and Taxes on Production and Imports
cannot exceed Output.
(Required) The Aggregation Scheme the model belongs to.

item.name: Impact Run
item.description: Run, cancel, and check the status of an impact analysis for a project.

item.name: Runs an impact analysis for a Project.

request.name: Runs an impact analysis for a Project.

description.content:
Starts the impact analysis for the given Project and returns the new Impact Run id, which is then
used to poll `GetImpactStatus`. If the Project has problems (missing events, invalid groups,
and so on) the response is a 400 (or 500) describing the issue.

The analysis runs in the background and is not complete when this call returns. A returned
run id on its own does not prove the run started - confirm it by checking that
`GetImpactStatus(runId)` returns a status and that `GetProject.lastImpactRunId` equals the
returned run id. Then poll `GetImpactStatus(runId)` until it reports `Complete` (treat
`Error` and `UserCancelled` as terminal failures) before reading results. Do not
poll the results reports (the economic-indicator or taxes report endpoints) to detect completion -
those reads are large and return errors until the run is finished. Poll every 30-60 seconds: simple
runs finish in a minute or two, large or MRIO analyses can take hours.

Before the run starts the Project is validated; the run requires all of the following:
- Group titles must be unique, and event titles must be unique.
- Every group must identify a Region - a region-less group is only caught here, not at create time.
- International (or US household) spending-pattern events must specify a spending-pattern Region.

For an MRIO Project the Groups have extra constraints: all Groups must use the same data year, no two
Groups may reference the same model, the Groups' Regions may not overlap or nest within one another,
any congressional-district Regions must be from the same Congress, and trade data must be available
between the Regions.

Caller-side requirement (not enforced server-side yet): set every group's `dollarYear` via
`CreateGroup`/`UpdateGroup` before running. A group missing it yields a run id that never
attaches - `GetImpactStatus` returns a bare 400 and `GetProject.lastImpactRunId` stays null.
(Required) The Project's identifier.

item.name: Gets the status of an impact analysis run.

request.name: Gets the status of an impact analysis run.

description.content:
Returns the overall status of the Impact Run, derived from its analyses. Possible values are
`New` (requested, not started), `InProgress`, `ReadyForWarehouse`, `Complete`,
`Error`, and `UserCancelled`.

This is the cheap endpoint to poll while an impact runs: treat anything that is not `Complete`
as not-ready and keep polling (roughly every 30-60 seconds), and treat `Error` and
`UserCancelled` as terminal failures. Only read the results reports once this reports
`Complete` - do not poll the results endpoints themselves to detect completion.

Note: for an unknown or never-attached run id this returns a bare 400 (and a 500 for some ids) with
no body, rather than a 404 or an `Error` status. Confirm the run actually started -
`GetProject.lastImpactRunId` equals the run id - before polling, and treat a bare 400/500 here
as "the run did not attach" (commonly a group missing its dollar year - see RunImpact), not a
transient error to retry.
(Required) The Impact Run identifier.
